new_entities.name: Beta-alanine supplementation
new_entities.description: Chronic beta-alanine supplementation intended to raise muscle carnosine and improve buffering during high-intensity exercise.

new_entities.name: Muscular endurance over 1 to 4 minutes
new_entities.description: Ability to sustain high-intensity muscular work in efforts lasting roughly one to four minutes.

edges.effect_quant: Meta-analytic evidence shows the clearest beta-alanine benefit in exercise lasting about 60 to 240 seconds, with pooled effect sizes small overall but larger for exercise-capacity tasks in that window.
edges.population: healthy adults and athletes performing sustained high-intensity exercise
edges.mechanism: Beta-alanine increases muscle carnosine, which improves intracellular buffering and should matter most when exercise acidosis becomes limiting. That makes the 1- to 4-minute duration window especially plausible biologically, and the pooled literature generally follows that prediction.
edges.summary: Beta-alanine is one of the better-supported buffering supplements, but its benefit is targeted rather than universal. The strongest signal is in high-intensity efforts lasting around one to several minutes, where a small average advantage appears reproducible across pooled studies.
edges.caveats: Not every sport-specific test improves, and some direct running protocols are null despite favorable meta-analytic trends. The literature is stronger for exercise-capacity style outcomes than for every real-world race or field-performance measure.
